GENERATE BURST VF-prim-fire-head-02 — painted primitive P01 HEAD / CORE — the projectile body of a fire bolt in flight for the fire treatment (Run C-5, E1: the fire projectile; architecture 03- § 2.3 build list). task_id "VF-prim-fire-head-02". One primitive per call. Paint the SHAPE REPRESENTING EMISSION only — light, glow, colour and motion are runtime layers.

IMAGE 1 is the SCALE + REGISTER board: a 1:1 native 512×512 crop of the painted cliffside clearing at the game camera with two figures 130 px tall (= 1 BH, body height) beside a 3× enlargement; everything is hand-drawn painted 2D — confident dark contour with taper, clean painted planes, restrained texture. IMAGE 2 is the APPROVED fire impact peak (E0-p; Matt-accepted): the fire VOCABULARY to match exactly — four flat greyscale value planes (near-black contour/rim, dark grey outer flame, light grey mid flame, white core), hooked tongues with hard plane edges, no gradients or glow. IMAGE 3 is the native ground crop alone (reading only).

Deliver EXACTLY ONE image, 512×512, GENUINELY TRANSPARENT background (RGBA: alpha 0 outside the body, opaque inside, no soft fringe wider than 1 px) — if transparency is impossible, a flat uniform #00ff00 plate and SAY SO. Content: the HEAD of a fire bolt travelling to the RIGHT (screen +x) — the PROJECTILE body, given the same care as the impact (Matt R-C5-109): a dense teardrop core with the blunt end LEADING on the right, a WHITE-HOT heart (the white plane) filling the leading half of the core so the bolt reads as a molten, glowing mass rather than a painted lick; three to four short hooked tongues sweeping back off the top and bottom edges toward the left, unequal; a hand-drawn dark contour with taper. PAINTED EXTENT: about 156 px across (1.2 BH) and about 110 px tall; centred; nothing touches the edge. FOUR flat greyscale planes, hard-edged: near-black contour, dark grey outer flame, light grey mid flame, WHITE core (≈ 40 % of the body). Deliver: out/fire_head_02.png.
RETURN: the receipt (task_id "VF-prim-fire-head-02"): images = integer; calls_used; status; concerns honestly.
